text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Generale des Eaux to ally with railway operator SNCF in telecommunications, competing with France Telecom.

-- Lagardere starts legal action at Council of State over aborted sale of Thomson SA to Lagardere in December. Prime Minister's office says move should not affect planned privatisation schedule for Thomson.

-- Budget deficit overshoot in 1996 was kept to 0.1 percent, at 4.1 percent of GDP. Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure, says in an interview that budget deficit must be brought down to 2 percent of GDP in order to reduce France's indebtedness.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe rules out authorizing cultivation in France of genetically-modified corn, but allows imports.
-- Foreigners' investments in France expected to create or save some 22,800 jobs in the next three years.
-- Franco-German helicopter group Eurocopter to sign a 2.5-billion-franc contract in Turkey.
-- Generale des Eaux expects a 40-billion-franc turnover in telecommunications industry by the year 2003.

-- Former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing in an interview says that Italy and Spain should be in the first wave of countries launching the European single currency, adds French interest rates can fall to German levels.
